definition: Of or pertaining to the hours before dawn; occurring in the dark period just before first light appears in the sky.
etymology: From Latin antelucanus, built from ante meaning before and lux, lucis meaning light. Roman writers used it to mark the quiet watches a person kept while the rest of the world still slept, those hours the ancients considered neither night nor quite morning.
usage: Late June compresses the antelucan hours almost to nothing; by the time the birds begin their first tentative notes, the eastern sky is already pale and committed to the day.
